athena.directive: Establish the Creative Liberation Engine as the sovereign, AI-native creative studio, empowering users with an infinitely extensible and deeply integrated suite of generative tools, driven by intelligent agents and a community-contributed ecosystem.
athena.rationale: The 'Flow' concept demonstrates the immense potential of an AI-powered creative studio. By adopting a similar vision, the Creative Liberation Engine can provide a self-hosted, comprehensive platform for creative professionals. This directive emphasizes sovereignty (Article I), complete implementations (Article IX), and a rich, extensible ecosystem, ensuring a powerful and future-proof creative environment.

options.title: The 'Google Flow Spatial Orchestrator' Strategy
options.description: Leverage Google Flow (labs.google/fx/tools/flow) as a high-fidelity Visual Synthesis and Cinema Engine rather than rebuilding a sovereign canvas from scratch. Integrate it by deploying the Creative Liberation Engine V6's Chrome-Agent (Playwright browser automation) to programmatically orchestrate the Google Flow canvas. Our specialized local agents (CURATOR, AURORA, DAVINCI) feed real-world sensor telemetry, script blueprints, and storyboards directly into Google Flow's Veo-powered video and ImageFX generation modules, pulling high-fidelity assets back into a sovereign, local timeline.
options.tradeoffs: Bypasses millions in custom canvas/rendering engineering costs and taps directly into Google's state-of-the-art Veo models. Relies on headed/headless browser session bridges, meaning we must manage active session cookies and credentials locally. Fully aligns with the V6 Strategic Thesis: Layer 1 is commodity AI rendering (Google Flow), Layer 2 is our sovereign moat (the reality model, spatial metadata, and post-production ontology).
options.architecture: Expose Google Flow as a high-fidelity Layer 1 rendering resource via a dedicated `mcp-google-flow` server. The CLE Chrome-Agent uses desktop-profile cookies to automate labs.google/fx/tools/flow—initiating projects, editing prompt nodes, framing camera sweeps, and executing script-to-video pipelines. Generated clip assets are harvested via local watchdogs, registered with the local Memory Spine, and cataloged in the Obsidian Vault.
options.design: A glassmorphic telemetry HUD inside NEXUS Command (`MatrixPanel` and `CanvasLayer`) running our Pitch Black Brutalist theme (#000000, #FF3366, #00FFCC). Shows live Google Flow automation logs ('Driving Google Flow: rendering Veo clip...', 'Veo node saturated, scaling local backup...') side-by-side with spatial telemetry and camera metadata graphs.

options.title: The 'Sovereign Canvas Prime' Strategy
options.description: Develop a foundational, highly extensible local-only multimodal creative canvas as the core of the Creative Liberation Engine's creative studio. This canvas will serve as the primary interface for all generative AI models and custom tools, focusing on a robust API and plug-in architecture.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant initial investment in developing a stable and performant core canvas engine and its API. There's a risk of becoming overly generic if not continuously refined with specific creative workflows in mind. Ensuring seamless integration of diverse generative models and maintaining real-time responsiveness will be a complex challenge.
options.architecture: A core, multimodal canvas engine with a robust API for integrating various generative models (text-to-image, text-to-video, multimodal) and custom tools. Prioritize a plug-in architecture for model wrappers and tool definitions. Implement a flexible data model for complex layered projects (e.g., assets, layers, timelines, effects). Agent orchestration will manage creative tasks and model calls on the canvas. Develop a high-performance rendering pipeline for diverse media types.
options.design: A minimalist, adaptable canvas UI that intelligently presents relevant tools and generative options based on context (e.g., selected layer, media type). Emphasis on direct manipulation (drag-and-drop, resizing, rotation) and intuitive visual feedback for generative processes. A 'smart' sidebar/panel that dynamically updates with agent suggestions, contextual parameter controls, and property inspectors. Implement a consistent visual language for layers, selections, and generative outputs.

options.title: The 'Agent-First Creative Partner' Strategy
options.description: Prioritize the development of a highly intelligent AI agent as the primary interaction model for creative workflows. This agent will act as a co-creator, guiding users, suggesting iterations, and executing complex generative commands through natural language.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant advancements in natural language understanding, creative reasoning, and proactive suggestion systems to deliver a truly intelligent and helpful agent. There's a potential for users to feel a lack of direct control if the agent becomes too prescriptive or if its suggestions aren't aligned with the user's vision. Initial user onboarding might be complex to establish trust and effective collaboration with the agent.
options.architecture: Develop a specialized 'Creative Agent' (e.g., a dedicated ATHENA sub-agent or a new agent) with deep contextual understanding of creative workflows, project goals, and user preferences. Implement advanced natural language processing (NLP) and generation (NLG) capabilities for conversational interaction. The agent will orchestrate generative models and custom tools, requiring robust internal APIs for agent access to all creative functionalities. Integrate a knowledge base for creative principles and best practices.
options.design: A conversational UI as the central interaction point, augmented by visual previews and direct manipulation controls on the canvas. The agent's dialogue will be presented clearly, with visual cues for agent activity, understanding, and progress. Implement a 'thought bubble' or 'suggestion panel' UI for agent explanations, rationale, and alternative creative directions. Provide clear mechanisms for users to accept, reject, or refine agent suggestions.

options.title: The 'Toolforge Ecosystem' Strategy
options.description: Emphasize the creation, sharing, and remixing of custom generative tools within the Creative Liberation Engine. This strategy focuses on building a robust platform for users to define and encapsulate their own AI-powered creative workflows.
options.tradeoffs: Requires a strong and engaged community to thrive; initial adoption and contribution might be slow. Significant effort needed to ensure the security and stability of user-generated tools, especially when dealing with arbitrary code or complex model interactions. The quality and usefulness of tools will vary, potentially leading to a fragmented user experience.
options.architecture: Build a robust 'Toolforge' platform including a visual programming environment (e.g., node-based editor or block-based scripting) for defining generative workflows and tool logic. Implement a secure sandbox environment for executing user-defined tools to prevent system vulnerabilities. Develop a decentralized registry or marketplace for sharing, discovering, and versioning community-contributed tools. Define a standardized tool definition format (e.g., JSON schema) for interoperability. Integrate with existing Creative Liberation Engine agents for tool discovery and recommendation.
options.design: A dedicated 'Toolforge' UI for building and testing tools, featuring a visual editor for workflow construction, parameter definition, and input/output mapping. A 'Tool Library' marketplace with robust search, filtering, rating, and categorization features for easy discovery. Clear visual indicators for tool provenance, creator, and security status. Provide comprehensive documentation, tutorials, and examples to encourage tool creation and sharing.

options.title: The 'Multimodal Media Weaver' Strategy
options.description: Focus on enabling seamless blending, transformation, and generation across diverse media types – text, images, audio, and video – within a unified creative environment.
options.tradeoffs: Extremely complex architectural challenge due to the inherent differences in media formats, processing requirements, and generative model types. Requires cutting-edge research and development in multimodal AI integration and cross-modal generation. Ensuring real-time performance and high fidelity across all media types can be resource-intensive.
options.architecture: Develop a unified media processing pipeline capable of ingesting, processing, and outputting text, images, audio, and video interchangeably. Implement advanced multimodal embedding techniques for semantic understanding across media. Build a robust cross-modal generation framework to enable transformations (e.g., text-to-image-to-video, audio-to-animation). Design a real-time rendering and previewing engine that can handle simultaneous display and manipulation of diverse media assets. Establish standardized data formats for multimodal project representation.
options.design: A unified timeline/canvas interface that intelligently adapts its controls and display based on the media types being worked with. Implement intuitive controls for cross-modal transformations (e.g., 'turn this image into a video clip', 'generate audio from this text prompt'). Develop visualizers for multimodal embeddings to help users understand the semantic relationships between different media elements. Ensure smooth transitions and consistent interaction patterns when switching between media contexts.

options.title: The 'Professional Control Suite' Strategy
options.description: Integrate traditional, professional-grade creative controls with AI-powered generative capabilities, aiming to augment existing workflows rather than completely redefine them. This provides a familiar yet enhanced experience for seasoned creatives.
options.tradeoffs: Can be challenging to seamlessly integrate traditional, deterministic editing tools with the probabilistic nature of generative AI without creating a disjointed or confusing user experience. Requires significant UI/UX design effort to balance the power and complexity of professional controls with the simplicity and magic of AI. Risk of feature bloat if not carefully curated.
options.architecture: Integrate existing robust open-source professional editing libraries (e.g., image manipulation, video editing, audio processing) and expose their functionalities through a standardized Creative Liberation Engine API. Develop a deep integration layer for generative models to augment these professional tools contextually (e.g., AI-powered selection, content-aware fill, style transfer as filters). Implement a modular architecture allowing users to enable/disable specific professional toolsets. Ensure robust undo/redo and version control for all operations.
options.design: A UI that skillfully blends familiar professional editing interfaces (e.g., Photoshop-like layers, Premiere-like timelines, granular parameter sliders) with AI-powered enhancements. Contextual AI suggestions and generative options appear within familiar tool panels or as overlay controls, rather than separate modules. Provide customizable workspaces and keyboard shortcuts to cater to professional user preferences. Maintain a high degree of visual fidelity and responsiveness for all professional controls.
